content.comment_body: Good morning, The [product_name] supports up to 8 analog inputs, but in the device settings under I/O, I can only enable 4 analog inputs (AI1 to AI4). I have two questions: 1. If I connect two [product_name] expansion modules, can I then enable all 8 analog inputs in I/O settings, or does the device just recognize the expansion modules’ inputs as AI5 to AI8? 2. The [product_name] expansion module is listed as supporting 8 digital inputs, 8 digital outputs, and 4 MW. Does this mean 4 MW refers to 4 analog inputs, and if I connect this module, can I use it in place of two analog expansion modules? Thanks in advance.

1.) In the I/O settings section, you only enable analog inputs for the base device. If you are not using any analog inputs on the base device, or if it has none, set the selection to 0. This leaves addresses AI1 to AI8 available for expansion modules. Setting it to 2 analog inputs means AI1 and AI2 are used for the base, and AI3 to AI8 for expansions. Setting it to 4 analog inputs means AI1 to AI4 are for the base, and AI5 to AI8 for expansions. 2.) The expansion module listed as DM16 24R only provides 8 digital inputs and 8 digital outputs. I'm not sure what you mean by "MW"...
Thank you. Please refer to picture 1 to see what I meant by MW. Do you know what the manufacturer means by 4 MW?
MW stands for module widths. 1 MW is equal to 18 mm; 4 MW equals 72 mm.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing confusion regarding how to enable the full range of analog inputs on the [product_name], particularly in the interaction between the main device and expansion modules in the I/O configuration interface. There is also uncertainty regarding specific terms used in documentation and interface, like 'MW', which causes misunderstandings about the capabilities and features of the expansion modules.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a clear and intuitive configuration process that makes it evident how to activate all analog inputs when additional modules are connected. They also want terminology in documentation and interfaces to be explained directly to prevent confusion.
